title: Establish the initial finding registry before repairs begin
description:
Create version 1 of the durable finding registry NOW — before any C-epic or
D-epic implementation starts. The registry is the instrument that keeps repairs
honest; if it is only assembled near closure it cannot govern the repairs it
exists to govern.

Registry v1 must carry, per row:
  * one canonical defect or invariant ID;
  * ALL aliases (see prefix table below);
  * status — accepted | rejected | narrowed | ambiguous | disclosed-dependency;
  * a GENERATED membership query (never a copied total);
  * owning bead;
  * pack boundary and engine boundary;
  * intended regression form.

DISPUTED AND NON-LITERAL FINDINGS — these are exactly why v1 must exist early:
  * sol:CAP-002 (condition/action/feat structural gaps) must be represented but
    marked NARROWED, not implemented literally. The 2026-07-24 independent audit
    verified conditions as exact against source; implementing CAP-002 literally
    would REGRESS already-correct typed condition effects.
  * The Fable language-set conclusion is an ADJUDICATION/POLICY issue, not a
    projection defect — represent it as such.
  * Conflicting half-damage and geometry counts across reviews (79 vs 77
    creature, 8 vs 9 hazard, 391 vs 399 engine:F5) must resolve to a GENERATED
    MEMBERSHIP QUERY. Never reconcile them by picking a number.

CANONICAL ALIAS PREFIXES — never a bare "F1" or "CAP-001":
  engine:F1 .. engine:F10     pack executionReadiness engineHooks[].engine families
  fable:F1 .. fable:F8        Fable 5 audit findings
  opus:F-01 .. opus:F-35      Opus 5 original + amended audit findings
  sol:CAP-001 .. sol:CAP-014  GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit findings
  indep:001 .. indep:012      independent review (formerly "SOL-001..012"; renamed
                              so it stops colliding with the sol: model-name prefix)

COUNT HYGIENE: every number in this bead is a SNAPSHOT at commit 4384f25. The
generated ledger/predicate is authoritative. No acceptance test may require a
hand-copied number (e.g. 391, 399, 77, 79).



## REVIEW CONTRACT

Protocol: eshyra-clause-review-v1

Revised 2026-07-26 after DECOMPOSITION, approved by the user. Supersedes the
previous contract on this bead, which recorded an open failure. Derived from
commit f75acb2.

### Source obligation
- Source membership: 68 canonical rows covering all 70 review aliases from
  indep:*, opus:F-*, sol:CAP-* and fable:F*.
- Membership derivation: SPLIT. A row is membershipStatus='derived' only when its
  baseline snapshot is reproducible by re-running its named query and matching
  the stored identities. Every other row is 'underived' and carries a per-row
  underivedReason plus owningDerivationBead=eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7.
  CURRENT STATE: 0 derived, 68 underived. No row currently establishes
  authority independently of the pack under repair, so none qualifies. That is
  the honest measure of what this artifact grounds.
- Source spans or authoritative inputs: obligation.authority must be independent
  of the pack under repair.
- Complete obligations covered: the MODEL and the gating are complete here.
  Deriving membership for prose-scoped rows is eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7 and is
  explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this PR.

### Pack or artifact representation
- Required semantic distinctions: target.kind in record|clause|field|path|
  relationship|capability with a structured selector, never a text search.
- Branches and alternatives: the ten required finding cases, verified by target
  kind and selector rather than by mere row existence.
- Timing, lifecycle, and termination: carried per finding.
- Provenance and ownership requirements: statusReasoning where status is not
  accepted; an owning repair bead; a regression form.

### Cross-kind and cross-surface checks
- Related kinds or subsystems: cross-kind findings use multi-family membership;
  target.kind=capability links engine findings to engine:F* families.
- Corpus-wide predicates or reconciliation: baselineMembership is a reproducible
  identity snapshot, distinct from generated current membership. The four
   half-damage 93.

### Engine capability
- Required capabilities: engine findings carry engineBoundary and
  target.kind=capability.
- Existing owner beads: eshyra-olc5 family epics.
- Known missing capability handling: routed through the owning repair bead.

### Reference execution or executable proof
- Real artifact or pack-driven scenarios: derived rows re-execute their query
  against the committed pack and must match the snapshot.
- Negative and fail-closed scenarios: findingRegistryClosureReady() returns
  false while any row is underived, naming them, tested in both directions;
  underivedReason may not be constant or template-derived; duplicate
  canonicalId rejected via a real Set; declared baseline member disappearance
  fails.
- Replay, rollback, or determinism requirements: bd owner checks skip gracefully
  when the binary is absent.

### Approved residuals
- Source ambiguities: none owned here.
- Deliberately model-adjudicated boundaries: indep:011 is an adjudication /
  policy extension point, status accepted with an escape-hatch regression.
- Explicitly unsupported scope: membership derivation for the 64 prose-scoped
  rows. This is DECLARED, machine-checkable, and blocks closure — it is not a
  silent gap. eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7 owns it and gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.2 and
  eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4.

### Closure evidence
- Generated membership query: per-row violation queries plus the baseline
  snapshot for derived rows; findingRegistryClosureReady() is the gate.
- Permanent regression evidence: packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts.
- Finding-registry aliases: this artifact IS the alias registry; all 70 aliases
  resolve to exactly one row.

### Material contract changes in this cycle
1. DECOMPOSED. Membership derivation for prose-scoped rows moved to
   eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7. Reason: two fresh full reviews found the same
   schema-conformant facade, and the boundary proved sharp — rows derivable by
   pack query were correct; rows needing audit-prose reconciliation were filled
   with an exemplar plus boilerplate. Those are different kinds of work.
2. exemplarJustification DELETED with its rule and test. Reason: a guard
   satisfiable by a single constant string across 61 rows is not a guard; it
   became the hiding place for the defect it was meant to prevent.
3. membershipStatus added with a mechanical classification rule that uses no
   judgement about finding scope: derived requires a reproducible query re-run.
4. underivedReason may not be constant or template-derived, enforced by test —
   the same technique that fixed the invariants.
5. findingRegistryClosureReady() added so an underived row FAILS the closure
   gate at eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4 instead of passing as an exemplar.

Prior review approval does NOT survive these changes. A fresh full review is
required.

### Rescope 2026-07-27 after the churn stop rule (head c73f6bc)

RETAINED SCOPE: the durable row model — obligation + target + invariant separated
from the transient violation; baseline distinct from generated current
membership; exact structured identities; membershipStatus with its mechanical
classification rule; 68 rows and 70 aliases each resolving once.
Capability targets now carry qualified engine:F1..F10 identities with primitive,
hook and owning bead (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.9, CLOSED, landed in c73f6bc), joinable
with the bootstrap capability ledger. Ownership is judged by actual bead identity
because the family epics retain historical eshyra-o9bd.19.5.* IDs.

DECOMPOSED OUT:
  eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7  derive exact audited membership for the 64 prose-scoped
                      rows. Corpus analysis, not registry construction.
  eshyra-o9bd.19.1.8  make violation predicates executable defect checks. The
                      queryId only SELECTS a row; every finding then runs the
                      same baseline-existence join, so wrong values, missing
                      branches, bad resets and lifecycle errors are never
                      evaluated and expectedAfterRepair is unused.

KNOWN OPEN DEFECTS IN THE RETAINED CORE — must be fixed for the rescope to mean
anything, and NOT yet assigned to a dispatch:
  * the anti-template guard is ineffective — reasons use a title-substitution
    template the validator does not catch, since it rejects only duplicates or
    reasons containing the canonical ID;
  * findingRegistryClosureReady() is FAIL-OPEN — it checks only whether rows say
    'derived' and never applies the executable-generator and snapshot
    validations directly below it, and the suite constructs an invalid
    all-derived registry and expects true.
See the cross-artifact fail-open note recorded on this bead: a closure predicate
must name the exact blocker set and assert blocker IDENTITIES, never a count.

### Invariant classes added 2026-07-27 (review at b738078)

Required by the churn-stop rule: the single-valued hook relation was a new
defect class, so this contract is updated and the next review is a FRESH FULL
review. Another new class in that review requires rescope or design reopening.

- **THE HOOK-TO-PRIMITIVE RELATION IS MULTI-VALUED.** A capability hook may span
  several canonical primitives and must map to all of them. Restricting it to
  one silently drops the others: engine:F10's currency/property/inventory/XP
  hook mapped only to currency mutation although the roster separately requires
  retained-asset creation; engine:F5 storage/charge/reset and engine:F9
  quantity-cost/area-targeting lose primitives the same way. A hook whose
  primitives cannot all be determined must fail closed, not pick one.
- **PACK SELF-DERIVATION IS INADMISSIBLE AND ENFORCED.** It is not enough to
  document that a pack query cannot establish authoritative membership — the
  validator must REJECT it. A registered pack generator may supply CURRENT
  membership for comparison; it may never be the authority that makes a row
  derived. Any test asserting that pack-generated rows stop blocking encodes the
  defect and must be changed.
- **JUSTIFICATION FIELDS ARE STRUCTURED, NOT PROSE.** The anti-template guard has
  now been evaded four times — an identical sentence across 61 rows, round-robin
  audit aliases, title-substituted reasons, and now a normalizer that excludes
  the newly introduced substitution fields while blacklisting the previous
  revision's exact sentences. Prose fields derived from a row's own metadata
  carry no independent information and will always be templatable, so hardening
  the detector is the wrong move. `underivedReason` becomes STRUCTURED: a closed
  enum of blocking causes plus a resolvable reference to the blocking artifact or
  bead. A structured value either resolves or does not; it cannot be paraphrased
  into looking distinct.

### Material contract changes in this cycle
1. Membership state corrected to 0 derived / 68 underived; the previous contract
   asserted 4/64 after the artifact had already changed. That staleness was a
   supervisor error, not an implementation drift.
2. Hook-to-primitive mapping is multi-valued and fails closed when
   indeterminate.
3. Pack self-derivation must be rejected by the validator, not merely
   discouraged in documentation.
4. Free-text justification replaced by structured cause plus resolvable
   reference.

Prior review approval does NOT survive these changes. A fresh full review is
required.

*** CROSS-ARTIFACT PATTERN 2026-07-27: FAIL-OPEN 'READY' PREDICATES ***
PR #476's findingRegistryClosureReady() and PR #477's ledger closure check were
built in separate rounds by separate dispatches, and BOTH shipped fail-open: each
reports readiness from a status field without applying the validations sitting
directly beneath it, and each has a test that constructs the invalid case and
expects true.

Treat fail-open as the DEFAULT failure mode of any 'ready'/'complete' helper in
this program. A closure predicate must prove the negative: name the exact blocker
set, assert blocker IDENTITIES rather than a count, and be tested in both
directions — not-ready on real data with real blockers, ready only on a fixture
where every blocker is resolved. A test pinning a COUNT of blockers passes
identically for a different set of the same size, which is how both of these
survived review.

Applies to the #476 rescope's retained fail-open gate and to eshyra-o9bd.19.1.8.
*** SUPERVISOR REVIEW MISSES 2026-07-27 ***
Two findings at 6a1b275 passed my own review and should not have. Recording the
mechanism, not just the fact.

1. CLOSURE SUBSET FIXTURE. I read the test that builds
   validFixture = registry.rows.filter(derived) and asserts ready===true, and
   called it 'a genuinely valid fixture'. Deleting the 64 unresolved obligations
   is the cheapest possible way to fake closure, and I blessed it. The lesson:
   when reviewing a gate, ask what the CHEAPEST way to make it green is, and
   check that path is blocked. A fixture that removes the failing inputs is
   always that path.

2. WEAK REGRESSION TEST OF MY OWN. I added 'rejects reasons that share a template
   across rows' using two rows whose text is byte-identical apart from an
   interpolated title. The guard already caught that. The data's actual pattern
   is a shared skeleton with PARAPHRASED subjects, which survives normalization.
   So my test passed against a case that was never at risk and created false
   confidence that the guard was protected. The lesson: a regression test must
   fail against the pattern PRESENT IN THE DATA, not against an idealized
   version of the defect. Before adding one, confirm it fails on the current
   implementation for the real reason.

Both are instances of the same reviewer error: verifying that a mechanism exists
rather than that it binds.
